query: The Test Flight Mir has built a flying machine with canvas wings and seven propellers. It is balanced on the edge of the north tower. "Brooms are so last century," they say, strapping in. "I need someone on the rope. Probably. Possibly." Hold the rope The machine flies — wobbly, loud, glorious — twice around the tower before landing in the lake. Mir surfaces whooping. You're both legends by dinner. The rope wins. You are dragged eight feet along the roof before letting go. The machine lands in a tree. Mir waves from it, delighted. Insist on a safety net You spend a day building a net. The machine flies four feet and drops into it. "Data!" says Mir happily. Nobody dies. It's a good day.
